string-array.name: splash_tips
string-array.item: Double-tap anywhere on the map to force the current area to reload. Handy when the display looks stuck or incomplete.
Long press the burger button to jump straight to your personal marks, without going through the menu.
In the marks list, a short tap selects a mark. A long press opens its editor.
Tap the speed at the bottom right to switch between km/h, mph and knots. Your choice is remembered.
Tap the heading readout to switch between true and magnetic north. The local declination is applied for you.
Tap the bearing panel at the top left to move to the next selected mark, from the nearest to the farthest.
The recentre button only shows up once you have panned the map, so only when it is of any use.
Long press the zone button to delete the watch zone. A short tap cycles through create, edit and validate.
Set the watch zone with two fingers: one for its angle, one for its size.
Pan the map and sighting reticles appear. Tap a reticle to drop a mark there, tap anywhere else to measure a distance leg by leg.
While measuring, the recentre button turns into a broom: it wipes the measurement chain and keeps you in pan mode.
Tap a mark that is alarming to mute it for the rest of the session. The flashing border stays as long as the danger does.
Panned far from home? The red marker on the edge of the screen points back to your real position, with the distance to it.
Flick the map and it keeps gliding, then slows down gently.
Swipe down from the top of the screen to bring the Android bar back.
Share a position from a message or a website and pick MyBuoy: the mark editor opens ready filled in.
A boat compass never shows true north. Store yours with its deviation curve and every heading is corrected for you.
A map download carries on in the background. Leave the app, the notification keeps you posted.
The avatar follows your pace: a boat on the water, a walker on land.
Everything works with no network at all. Download the map once, then forget about coverage.
Server addresses live in the advanced settings. You can run your own map server.
Alarm distances and delays, coordinate format, track display and avatar all live in the Parameters page.
MyBuoy has no ads, no tracking and no budget. Word of mouth is the whole marketing department.
Fund the project and get an avatar drawn to your own brief, yours alone.
Fund the project and get a personal mark icon made to your taste.
MyBuoy is free software under the AGPL-3.0. The full source is public: read it, build it, fork it.
Every release is announced on the Telegram channel, with the changelog and the download link.
The maps, the roads and the seamarks all come from OpenStreetMap, surveyed by hundreds of thousands of volunteers.
You can help with code, with field testing, or with money. All three matter.
